subject: c12-eng
scope: CBSE Class XII English Core (301) 2026-27 written/theory Board-exam preparation; internal assessment (Listening, Speaking and Project Work) excluded for the private-candidate scope.

weightage.label: Literature Text Book and Supplementary Reading Text

c12-eng-01.name: Reading Skills
tips: Practise both prescribed unseen-passage types: literary/factual/descriptive and case-based factual passages with verbal/visual input.
Answer from the passage first; use general knowledge only when it is not being substituted for textual evidence.
For inference questions, state the inference and connect it to the relevant textual clue.
For case-based passages, read charts/statistical input carefully before answering.
Practise vocabulary through inference rather than isolated word memorisation.
mistakes: Answering from general knowledge instead of passage evidence.
Confusing inference with a copied sentence.
Overlooking visual/statistical information in a case-based passage.

c12-eng-02.name: Creative Writing Skills
tips: Maintain a separate format checklist for each prescribed writing task.
Keep notice and invitation/reply responses within 50 words.
Keep job applications, letters to the editor, articles and reports within 120–150 words.
Use the verbal/visual input supplied in the question rather than inserting memorised material.
Check format, organisation, tone, required information and word limit before submitting.
mistakes: Incorrect format or missing required parts.
Exceeding or falling materially short of the prescribed word range.

c12-eng-03.name: Flamingo Prose
tips: Read each prescribed prose text completely and track important incidents, themes and character/event development.
Prepare extract-based comprehension and interpretation questions separately from longer analytical answers.
For 40–50-word answers, answer the exact question with concise, evidence-linked inference.
For 120–150-word answers, develop an analytical/evaluative response rather than retelling the chapter.
Use relevant incidents, events and textual references as support.
mistakes: Retelling the whole chapter instead of answering the exact question.
Making character/theme claims without textual support.
Writing long answers without analytical or evaluative development.

c12-eng-04.name: Flamingo Poetry
tips: Revise the central idea and important images of every prescribed poem.
Prepare for extract questions involving comprehension, interpretation, analysis, inference and appreciation.
Identify relevant poetic features, but explain their effect or connection to meaning when required.
Use the poem's own images and ideas as evidence rather than generic poetry commentary.
Practise concise answers that directly connect the poetic detail to the question.
mistakes: Identifying a poetic feature without explaining its effect when analysis is required.
Giving a generic theme instead of interpreting the supplied extract.
Using memorised commentary that does not address the question.

c12-eng-05.name: Vistas / Supplementary Reading
tips: Read all prescribed Vistas texts for global comprehension rather than only memorising summaries.
Practise prose extracts and 40–50-word inferential answers separately.
For 120–150-word responses, use relevant incidents, events and themes as reference points.
Distinguish inference from direct textual detail when explaining an incident or character.
Practise analytical/evaluative questions that require understanding across the text.
mistakes: Giving a chapter summary instead of answering the analytical question.
Making claims without linking them to an incident, event or theme.
Ignoring the exact wording of the question while recalling a memorised answer.

order: Finish Reading Skills first: practise both unseen-passage types and train specifically for comprehension, interpretation, analysis, inference, evaluation and vocabulary through inference.
Build separate format checklists for notice, formal/informal invitation and reply, job application with bio-data/resume, letter to the editor, article and report.
Practise all writing tasks within their prescribed word limits: up to 50 words for notice/invitation-reply and 120–150 words for letters, articles and reports.
Read all prescribed Flamingo prose and poetry actively, tracking central ideas, important incidents/images, themes and the textual evidence needed for inferential and analytical responses.
Read all prescribed Vistas texts for global comprehension, then practise incident/theme-based analytical and evaluative answers.
Practise extract questions separately for Flamingo poetry, Flamingo prose and Vistas prose because the assessed competencies differ slightly by source.
Practise 40–50-word literature short answers with direct, evidence-linked inference rather than chapter summaries.
Practise 120–150-word literature answers with analytical/evaluative development and relevant incidents, events, themes or extracts as reference points.
Finish with timed mixed-section papers using the current 22 + 18 + 40 theory structure, then review mistakes by comprehension, format, expression, evidence and interpretation.
Keep Listening, Speaking and Project Work separate from written-theory preparation.

prescribed_text_reference.label: Section A — Reading Skills
prescribed_text_reference.text: Practise both prescribed unseen-passage types: one unseen passage that may be factual, descriptive or literary, and one unseen case-based factual passage using verbal/visual inputs such as statistical data or charts. The combined word limit for the two passages is 700–750 words. Focus on comprehension, interpretation, analysis, inference, evaluation and vocabulary through inference.

prescribed_text_reference.label: Section B — Notice Writing
prescribed_text_reference.text: Practise the prescribed notice-writing format and keep the response within the stated limit of up to 50 words. Make every required piece of information explicit and do not add irrelevant material.

prescribed_text_reference.label: Section B — Formal/Informal Invitation and Reply
prescribed_text_reference.text: Practise both formal and informal invitation/reply formats. Keep each response within 50 words and make sure the response type matches the prompt.

prescribed_text_reference.label: Section B — Application for a Job with Bio-data/Resume
prescribed_text_reference.text: Practise the prescribed job-application format using the given verbal/visual input. Keep the letter within 120–150 words and include the requested bio-data or resume component without adding unrelated information.

prescribed_text_reference.label: Section B — Letter to the Editor
prescribed_text_reference.text: Practise letters to the editor based on verbal/visual input and public-interest issues. The prescribed purpose is to give suggestions or opinion. Keep the response within 120–150 words and maintain the required formal structure.

prescribed_text_reference.label: Section B — Article Writing
prescribed_text_reference.text: Practise article writing in 120–150 words. Questions are based on verbal input and may be descriptive or analytical. Organise the response around the given subject rather than inserting memorised material.

prescribed_text_reference.label: Section B — Report Writing
prescribed_text_reference.text: Practise report writing in 120–150 words. Questions are based on verbal input and may be descriptive or analytical. Keep the report focused on the information supplied by the question.

prescribed_text_reference.label: Section C — Literature question types
prescribed_text_reference.text: Prepare for poetry extracts from Flamingo, prose extracts from Vistas and Flamingo, 40–50-word short answers, and 120–150-word long answers. Literature questions assess comprehension, interpretation, analysis, inference, evaluation, appreciation, critical thinking and extrapolation beyond/across the text. For long answers, use incidents, events, themes, passages or extracts from the prescribed texts as relevant reference points.

prescribed_text_reference.label: Flamingo — The Last Lesson
prescribed_text_reference.text: Revise the complete text for extract-based comprehension and interpretation, short inferential responses, and analytical/evaluative long-answer questions. Be able to connect relevant incidents and themes directly to the question.

prescribed_text_reference.label: Flamingo — Lost Spring
prescribed_text_reference.text: Revise the complete text for extract-based comprehension and interpretation, short inferential responses, and analytical/evaluative long-answer questions. Use relevant incidents and themes as evidence rather than retelling the whole text.

prescribed_text_reference.label: Flamingo — Deep Water
prescribed_text_reference.text: Revise the complete text for extract-based comprehension and interpretation, short inferential responses, and analytical/evaluative long-answer questions. Build answers from relevant incidents and the text's development rather than memorised summaries.

prescribed_text_reference.label: Flamingo — The Rattrap
prescribed_text_reference.text: Revise the complete text for extract-based comprehension and interpretation, short inferential responses, and analytical/evaluative long-answer questions. Support interpretations with relevant incidents, themes and events from the text.

prescribed_text_reference.label: Flamingo — Indigo
prescribed_text_reference.text: Revise the complete text for extract-based comprehension and interpretation, short inferential responses, and analytical/evaluative long-answer questions. Practise connecting the question to relevant incidents and themes.

prescribed_text_reference.label: Flamingo — Poets and Pancakes
prescribed_text_reference.text: Revise the complete text for prose extract questions, inferential short answers and analytical/evaluative long answers. Keep responses tied to relevant incidents, observations and themes from the prescribed text.

prescribed_text_reference.label: Flamingo — The Interview
prescribed_text_reference.text: Revise the complete text for prose extract questions, inferential short answers and analytical/evaluative long answers. Distinguish direct textual evidence from inference when answering.

prescribed_text_reference.label: Flamingo — Going Places
prescribed_text_reference.text: Revise the complete text for prose extract questions, inferential short answers and analytical/evaluative long answers. Answer the exact question using relevant incidents, events and themes.

prescribed_text_reference.label: Flamingo Poetry — My Mother at Sixty-Six
prescribed_text_reference.text: Prepare for a poetry extract with comprehension, interpretation, analysis, inference and appreciation. Revise the poem's central ideas, important images and relevant poetic features, and explain their connection to meaning when asked.

prescribed_text_reference.label: Flamingo Poetry — Keeping Quiet
prescribed_text_reference.text: Prepare for a poetry extract with comprehension, interpretation, analysis, inference and appreciation. Revise central ideas, important images and relevant poetic features, and connect them to the question.

prescribed_text_reference.label: Flamingo Poetry — A Thing of Beauty
prescribed_text_reference.text: Prepare for a poetry extract with comprehension, interpretation, analysis, inference and appreciation. Revise central ideas, important images and relevant poetic features, explaining their effect where required.

prescribed_text_reference.label: Flamingo Poetry — A Roadside Stand
prescribed_text_reference.text: Prepare for a poetry extract with comprehension, interpretation, analysis, inference and appreciation. Revise central ideas, important images and relevant poetic features, and support answers with textual reference.

prescribed_text_reference.label: Flamingo Poetry — Aunt Jennifer's Tigers
prescribed_text_reference.text: Prepare for a poetry extract with comprehension, interpretation, analysis, inference and appreciation. Revise central ideas, important images and relevant poetic features, and explain their connection to meaning.

prescribed_text_reference.label: Vistas — The Third Level
prescribed_text_reference.text: Prepare for prose extracts, 40–50-word inferential questions and 120–150-word analytical/evaluative questions. For long answers, use relevant incidents, events and themes and show global comprehension of the text.

prescribed_text_reference.label: Vistas — The Tiger King
prescribed_text_reference.text: Prepare for prose extracts, 40–50-word inferential questions and 120–150-word analytical/evaluative questions. Build answers from relevant incidents, events and themes rather than a memorised chapter summary.

prescribed_text_reference.label: Vistas — Journey to the End of the Earth
prescribed_text_reference.text: Prepare for prose extracts, 40–50-word inferential questions and 120–150-word analytical/evaluative questions. Demonstrate global comprehension and use relevant textual incidents, events and themes.

prescribed_text_reference.label: Vistas — The Enemy
prescribed_text_reference.text: Prepare for prose extracts, 40–50-word inferential questions and 120–150-word analytical/evaluative questions. Support interpretations with relevant incidents, events and themes from the text.

prescribed_text_reference.label: Vistas — On the Face of It
prescribed_text_reference.text: Prepare for prose extracts, 40–50-word inferential questions and 120–150-word analytical/evaluative questions. Keep responses tied to the prescribed text and use relevant incidents and themes.

prescribed_text_reference.label: Vistas — Memories of Childhood
prescribed_text_reference.text: Prepare both prescribed parts—The Cutting of My Long Hair and We Too are Human Beings—for prose-based questions. Practise inferential short answers and analytical/evaluative long answers using relevant incidents, events and themes.
